questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Mauritania?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mauritania article.

questions.proof: The capital city, which is also the biggest city in the country, is Nouakchott.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Mauritania?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Mauritania on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Berber languages” part of the Mauritania article.

questions.proof: In the south Zenaga is spoken and close to the border with Mali in the southeast Tamasheq (a variety of Tuareg) is spoken.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Mauritania?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Afro-Asiatic languages” part of the Mauritania article.

questions.proof: Modern Standard Arabic is the official language of Mauritania.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “At 1,030,700 km² (397,929 mi²), Mauritania is the world's 29th-largest country (after _____).”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “country”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mauritania article.

questions.proof: At 1,030,700 km² (397,929 mi²), Mauritania is the world's 29th-largest country (after Bolivia).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “As Mauritania is a former colony of _____, it is now part of the Francophonie.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “colony”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Mauritania article, under the heading “Foreign languages”.

questions.proof: As Mauritania is a former colony of France, it is now part of the Francophonie.
